We build these nuclear arsenals, but as Fukushima ably teaches, many if not most of these power plants are potential weapons in their own right.

We are barely able to maintain these plants even during peacetime and when our economies are running. What happens when suddenly civilization skips a beat? What happens to places like Hanford or the WIPP in New Mexico, when, for instance, we suffer some kind of monetary crisis as the result of the dollar collapsing?

History teaches us that civilizations come, and go. Ours is the first that says, we're last. Our civilization falls, and no one will be there, or able, to pick up all of the pieces left behind by our nuclear regimes.

Nobody is going to survive hundreds of spent fuel pools falling into disrepair.

And yet we continue to aim missiles at potential rivals. To what point? We're going to threaten a Russia or a China with destruction? Has it occurred to anyone that all they have to do is adopt a scorched earth policy with respect to their own nuclear properties to ward off such insanity? MIRVs are redundant in a world that will soon own five-hundred doomsday machines.

How does an anti-ballistic missile system shoot down hot particles of plutonium that get dispersed into the atmosphere when rods of mixed oxide burn and spew and contaminate and sow a legacy of ruin that will last for countless generations?

This is the world into which the madmen who court the second cold war will throw us. Whatever insignificant gain they imagine they achieve by punishing Putin for, say, arming Iran with defensive weaponry, or negotiating the unilateral disarmament of Syria's WMD stockpile, or continuing the Ponzi scheme that is private central banking, pales in comparison with the unprecedented costs we all will bear when it all fails.

We were, perhaps, at a moment where we were considering mothballing our nuclear industry, where instead of building new power plants we would instead spend capital on dismantling the old ones and the cleanup that must follow. But the logic of cold war two will hold that we need to maintain our stockpiles of things like cesium and plutonium and uranium.

The logic of cold war two holds that future generations are forfeit. And our silence in the face of that amounts to nothing less than total surrender before what can only be described as unadulterated evil.
